metadata.note: The Clinchfield -- the Carolina, Clinchfield and Ohio Railway and, after the 1924 Atlantic Coast Line / Louisville and Nashville joint lease, the Clinchfield Railroad -- running 277 miles from Elkhorn City, KY through Kingsport and Erwin, TN and Marion, NC to Spartanburg, SC. Added 2026-08-26 in answer to the question of why Kingsport, TN had no passenger rail on this map: it did, and this was it. The Clinchfield was a coal railroad that never pretended to be a passenger route -- one local each way, nearly 100 stops, ten hours end to end -- but it is the reason Kingsport exists as an industrial city, and its 1916 station is still the landmark at the foot of Broad Street. Drawn 1909-1954, from the year through service began to the year it ended. Split into two features on identical geometry at the December 1, 1924 change of operator, per CLAUDE.md Rule 4.
metadata.kingsport_other_operators: The Clinchfield was Kingsport's only scheduled passenger railroad. The Charleston, Cincinnati and Chicago ('Triple C') was graded through Kingsport in 1887-89 but was never completed or operated. The Holston River Railroad, later Southern Railway and now Norfolk Southern, skirts the town but is industrial and freight-only, so under CLAUDE.md Rule 1 it is not drawn.
metadata.not_drawn_santa_train: CSX's Santa Train has run the 110 miles from Shelbiana, KY to Kingsport every year since 1943, on the Saturday before Thanksgiving, and is the only passenger train that still reaches Kingsport. It is deliberately NOT drawn: members of the public do not ride it -- it carries volunteers and guests who throw gifts to crowds trackside -- so a line drawn 1943-2026 would assert a passenger service that is not available to passengers. Recorded here as context, per CLAUDE.md Rule 1's distinction between mentioning and asserting.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: The 1950 boundary between the two Clinchfield Railroad segments is a guess at when the service thinned from two trains each way to one; no timetable was consulted. All headway_min values are estimates. The 1954 end date is given consistently by Wikipedia, clinchfield.org and the Kingsport station histories, but one source phrases it as 'by 1954' and another as 'ended in 1954', so the last year of operation could be 1953. Whether the CC&O's own trains reached Spartanburg's Union Station over Southern rails, and over exactly which trackage, has not been verified -- the last 1.25 km into Spartanburg is not drawn.
metadata.source: Wikipedia (Clinchfield Railroad); clinchfield.org (passenger trains, Kingsport destination page); Tennessee Encyclopedia (Carolina, Clinchfield and Ohio Railway); appalachian-railroads.org (Railroads of Kingsport, Tennessee); Clio / SAH Archipedia (Clinchfield Railroad Station, Kingsport). Geometry from OpenStreetMap -- see each feature's geometry_source.

properties.line: Carolina, Clinchfield and Ohio: Elkhorn City – Spartanburg
properties.speed_source: Computed, not estimated: the through local covered the 277-mile route in slightly over 10 hours (No. 38 southbound 10h15m, No. 37 northbound 10h20m), which is ~27 mph / 43 km/h including nearly 100 scheduled and flag stops. Source: clinchfield.org's passenger-trains page. This is a whole-route average and says nothing about track speed between stops.
properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap, not approximated: no straight-line legs. Shortest-path routing over the ways of OSM route relations 2253414 (CSX 'Kingsport Subdivision', Elkhorn City-Kingsport-Erwin) and 2253405 (CSX 'Blue Ridge Subdivision', Erwin-Spartanburg); 267 of the 276 member ways carry old_railway_operator=Clinchfield, which is the proof the trace stayed on this company's rails. One dangling way-end was bridged with a connector under 10 m; no other gap was bridged. Douglas-Peucker simplified at 20 m to 1098 points, with the point nearest each named station force-kept. Traced 272.5 mi Elkhorn City-Spartanburg against the 277 route miles the timetables document; the ~4 mi shortfall is almost all at the south end, where the OSM relation stops 1.25 km short of Spartanburg's Union Station (the Clinchfield's passenger trains ran in over the Southern's rails for that last stretch, which is outside both relations and is NOT drawn). Station-by-station fit: Elkhorn City 430 m, Haysi 189 m, St. Paul 185 m, Kingsport 214 m, Erwin 89 m, Spruce Pine 202 m, Chesnee 362 m; Marion and Forest City land ~2.1 km from the town centroids I measured against, which is depot-vs-downtown offset, not a routing error. One 2,395 m chord near milepost 31 is NOT a straight-line approximation: it is the Sandy Ridge Tunnel, which OSM maps as a two-node way, and its length matches the tunnel's documented 7,854 ft almost exactly. 42 of the ways in the trace are tagged as tunnels. CAVEAT (CLAUDE.md Rule 2): this is the MODERN CSX alignment drawn back to 1909. The Clinchfield was built in one piece in 1908-09 and has seen little relocation, so the era mismatch is small, but it has not been checked line-by-line against a period valuation map. NOTE: the line does not pass through Dante, VA -- Dante was the Clinchfield's coal-operations hub on a branch about 13 km off this main line, and that branch is freight-only and so is not drawn (CLAUDE.md Rule 1).

segments.note: The Carolina, Clinchfield and Ohio completed its through line from Elkhorn City, KY to Spartanburg, SC in 1909 and began passenger service the same year -- the service that put Kingsport, TN on the passenger map. It ran as a local, never a through express: Nos. 37 (northbound) and 38 (southbound) covered the full 277 miles in a little over ten hours with nearly 100 stops, some scheduled and some by flag, while Nos. 36 and 39 worked the northern end between Elkhorn City and Erwin in about 6.5 hours. Kingsport's Clinchfield station, the clock-towered Clinton McKenzie building at the foot of Broad Street, opened in 1916 and was the town's passenger, mail and express depot. headway_min of 720 stands for roughly two trains each way per day and is an estimate, not read off a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: the 1909 service start, the train numbers and running times, and the 1916 Kingsport station date are each carried by the references below; the headway figure is NOT sourced.

segments.note: Operation passed to the Clinchfield Railroad on December 1, 1924, the Atlantic Coast Line and the Louisville and Nashville taking the CC&O under a joint lease; the corporate CC&O survived on paper until the 1983 Seaboard System merger, but the trains were the Clinchfield's from 1924. Passenger service continued as a local over the same route. headway_min of 1440 stands for about one train each way per day and is an estimate; the exact year the service thinned from two trains to one is NOT sourced, so the 1950 boundary below is approximate.
sources: Segment-level: the December 1 1924 lease date and operator change are sourced below. The headway and the 1950 era boundary are NOT sourced.

segments.note: By the 1950s the Clinchfield was down to a single daily train that alternated direction, worked by one diesel with a steam generator, and in the final years it ran only three times a week each way. Passenger service ended in 1954 -- Kingsport's station went vacant, and was restored in 1995 as a bank branch. No scheduled passenger train has served Kingsport since. headway_min of 2880 stands for roughly three round trips a week and is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: the single-train / three-times-weekly operation and the 1954 end date are sourced below (Wikipedia and clinchfield.org give 1954; the Kingsport station histories agree). The headway figure and the 1950 start of this era are NOT sourced.
